title: President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, celebrates Raksha Bandhan with students from schools across the country at Rashtrapati Bhavan
subtitle:
Students from 17 states, one Union Territory, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti participate in the special celebration
Students visit Pradhan Mantri Sangrahalaya, Rashtrapati Bhavan and Amrit Udyan as part of the educational experience
body_text:
President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today urged school students to extend the core values of Rakshabandhan, that is, love, care and protection, to the environment. She added that the Festival symbolized a bond of love that could be shared with anyone including family members, friends and even trees. She was celebrating Raksha Bandhan with students from schools across the country at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Expressing concern at the deteriorating balance of the environment, the President asked students to tie rakhis on plants and trees to preserve the equilibrium necessary for survival. Emphasizing that students were the future of the country, she said that the resolve taken to plant and nurture trees should become a lifelong commitment.
122 participants, including 89 students and 32 teachers participated in the special celebration. 13 Children with Special Needs (CwSN) were among the representatives drawn from 17 states, one Union Territory, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS).
As part of their visit to the national capital, the students visited Pradhan Mantri Sangrahalaya on August 27, 2026. Following the programme at Rashtrapati Bhavan today, the students also participated in a guided tour of Rashtrapati Bhavan and Amrit Udyan. They will also visit "The Light and the Lotus: Relics of the Awakened One" exhibition, which is currently being hosted at the Raipithora Cultural Complex, to view the sacred Buddha relics on display. They will further visit the National Science Centre, National War Memorial and India Gate as part of their educational visit on August 29, 2026.

enrichment.summary: President Droupadi Murmu celebrated Raksha Bandhan with 122 participants, including 89 students and 32 teachers (13 with special needs) from 17 states, one Union Territory, KVS and NVS, at Rashtrapati Bhavan. She urged students to extend the values of love and protection to the environment by tying rakhis on trees. The students also toured Pradhan Mantri Sangrahalaya, Amrit Udyan, and have further visits planned to a Buddha relics exhibition, National Science Centre, National War Memorial and India Gate.
enrichment.context: This is a ceremonial event at Rashtrapati Bhavan intended to foster national integration and environmental awareness among school students through a cultural festival. Such events are routinely organized by the President's Secretariat to engage students from diverse regions, including Kendriya Vidyalayas and Navodaya Vidyalayas, in cultural and educational tours of the capital's landmarks.
